genxml.title: National Semiconductor PC87307 Super I/O (marked NS87307) as wired in the Visual Workstation 320 and 540
genxml.doc: Register contract of the PC87307 Super I/O: its configuration protocol, the nine logical devices' configuration registers, the GPIO ports and the power management block, from the published datasheet, with the board's use taken from the system firmware, the Windows NT hardware abstraction layer and the Linux Visual Workstation code. Every register is eight bits wide. Grades: established means a datasheet page states it (the page is cited) or the shipped firmware and HAL do it in a routine read in full, which is a software expectation and not a measurement; inferred means a reasoned reading; unknown means no held source settles it. The configuration registers are addressed by an index written to an index port, so the offsets of the card, logical-device, chip-select and power management spaces are indexes, not bus addresses. The part has two variants: the PC87307 reads 0xc0 in its identification register and the PC97307 0xcf, and the PC97307 adds a stepping register; which one the board carries is not known. Not listed: the keyboard, mouse, real-time clock and advanced power control function registers, the floppy controller, UART and parallel port function registers, which are standard PC parts at the bases the logical devices select.

struct.name: PNP_RD_DATA
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.27
struct.doc: Plug and Play set RD_DATA port, used only by the Plug and Play ISA protocol. Bits 1 and 0 are fixed at 11.

struct.name: PNP_ISOLATION
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.27
struct.doc: Plug and Play serial isolation, used only by the Plug and Play ISA protocol.

struct.name: CFG_CONTROL
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.27, 30
struct.doc: Configuration control, write only, self-clearing. Bit 0 resets all logical devices and restores the configuration registers to their reset values (the soft reset); bit 1 returns the cards to the Wait for Key state and bit 2 resets the card select number, both only meaningful in Plug and Play ISA mode.

struct.name: PNP_WAKE
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.27
struct.doc: Plug and Play Wake[CSN], write only.

struct.name: PNP_RESOURCE
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.27
struct.doc: Plug and Play resource data, read only.

struct.name: PNP_STATUS
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.27
struct.doc: Plug and Play status, read only.

struct.name: CSN
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.27, 30
struct.doc: Card select number, used by the Plug and Play ISA protocol.

struct.name: LDN
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.27, 30
struct.doc: Logical device number: selects which logical device's registers the indexes 0x30 to 0xff address. The HAL writes 0, 5, 6, 3, 4 and 1 to steer IRQs 1, 3, 4, 6, 7 and 12; the PROM and Linux write 7 and 8 to set the GPIO and power management bases.

struct.name: SID
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.34
struct.doc: Identification. In the PC87307 bits 7:5 are the chip identification and bits 4:0 the revision, and the register reads 0xc0. In the PC97307 all eight bits are the chip identification and it reads 0xcf. Reset 0xc0 is the PC87307's. The reset of 0xc0 is inferred on the reading that the board part is a PC87307 (the board's documents say NS87307).

struct.name: SIOC1
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.34-35
struct.doc: SuperI/O configuration 1. Reset is 0x04, 0x06, 0x14 or 0x16 depending on the SELCS and CFG1 straps, whose board settings are not known. A soft reset has no effect.

struct.name: SIOC2
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.35
struct.doc: SuperI/O configuration 2. Reset is 0x00 to 0x03: bits 1:0 reflect the base address straps (11 is the 0x2e pair). The datasheet says the BIOS may switch the index and data ports to the Plug and Play addresses by changing these bits. A soft reset has no effect.

struct.name: CS_INDEX
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.35-36
struct.doc: Programmable chip select configuration index: the second-level index of the chip select register that the data register reaches. Bits 7:4 read 0.

struct.name: CS_DATA
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.36
struct.doc: Programmable chip select configuration data: the register named by the index above.

struct.name: SRID
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.36
struct.doc: Chip revision identification, PC97307 only: incremented on each tapeout.

struct.name: CFG_INDEX
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.24-25
struct.doc: Configuration index register. A write selects the configuration register the data port then reaches; a read returns the last index written. Reset: the part wakes in the Config state in PnP motherboard mode, so no key sequence is needed. The PROM and Linux write ports 0x2e and 0x2f directly. The reset value is unknown: no source states it and no PROM read of the index port before its first write is held.

struct.name: CFG_DATA
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.24-25
struct.doc: Configuration data register: reads and writes the register selected by the index. Reserved bits must be preserved, so software uses read-modify-write.

struct.name: CS_BASE_MSB
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.39-40
struct.doc: CS0, CS1 and CS2 base address, most significant byte (second-level indexes 0x00, 0x04 and 0x08).

struct.name: CS_BASE_LSB
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.39-40
struct.doc: CS0, CS1 and CS2 base address, least significant byte (indexes 0x01, 0x05, 0x09).

struct.name: CS_CONFIG
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.39-40
struct.doc: CS0, CS1 and CS2 configuration (indexes 0x02, 0x06, 0x0a). The board's use of the chip selects is not known.

struct.name: P1_DATA
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.170
struct.doc: Port 1 data. A read returns the pin for an input bit and the latch for an output bit; a write latches the value and drives output pins only. The write latch resets to 0xff. The firmware and Linux read this byte at the GPIO base after enabling the block.

struct.name: P1_DIR
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.170-171
struct.doc: Port 1 direction: 0 input, 1 output.

struct.name: P1_OTYPE
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.170-171
struct.doc: Port 1 output type: 0 open-drain, 1 push-pull.

struct.name: P1_PULLUP
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.170-171
struct.doc: Port 1 pull-up control: 0 none, 1 internal pull-up.

struct.name: P2_DATA
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.170-171
struct.doc: Port 2 data, as port 1.

struct.name: P2_DIR
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.170-171
struct.doc: Port 2 direction.

struct.name: P2_OTYPE
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.170-171
struct.doc: Port 2 output type.

struct.name: P2_PULLUP
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.170-171
struct.doc: Port 2 pull-up control.

struct.name: P1_LOCK
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.171
struct.doc: Port 1 lock. Bits 7 and 6 lock the direction and pull-up bits of GPIO17 and GPIO16, and for outputs the pin value and buffer type. Only a hardware (master) reset clears them. Bits 5:0 are reserved; offsets 0x01 to 0x07 of this bank are reserved.

struct.name: LD0_ACTIVATE
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.30 Table 2-12
struct.doc: Activate (bit 0). The PROM activates it; the HAL selects it to steer IRQ 1. Reset 0 or 1 according to the CFG0 strap (the board's strap is not known); the device is active only when its function enable bit in the power management block is also set.

struct.name: LD0_IORC
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.30 Table 2-12
struct.doc: I/O range check: bit 0 chooses the byte the device drives (0xaa or 0x55) and bit 1 enables the check, valid only while the device is inactive. Bits 7:2 read 0.

struct.name: LD0_BASE_MSB
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.30 Table 2-12
struct.doc: Base address bits 15:8.

struct.name: LD0_BASE_LSB
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.30 Table 2-12
struct.doc: Base address bits 7:0; the low bits are read only and the decoder ignores them.

struct.name: LD0_CMD_BASE_MSB
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.30 Table 2-12
struct.doc: Command window base address bits 15:8.

struct.name: LD0_CMD_BASE_LSB
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.30 Table 2-12
struct.doc: Command window base address bits 7:0; bit 2 reads 1. The reset reads 0x64 (the table prints it as 64).

struct.name: LD0_IRQ
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.30 Table 2-12
struct.doc: Interrupt select: bits 3:0 give the IRQ line, 1 to 15, 0 means none. The part offers IRQ 1, 3 to 12, 14 and 15. The HAL writes the interrupt type register only; Linux 2.2 writes this one on a 320 revision 5 board.

struct.name: LD0_IRQ_TYPE
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.30 Table 2-12
struct.doc: Interrupt type: bit 0 edge (0) or level (1), bit 1 polarity, low with an open-drain output (0) or high with a push-pull output (1). Which bits are writable depends on the device. The HAL's steering writes bits 0 and 1 of this register for IRQs 1, 3, 4, 6, 7 and 12, and only on the no-8259 route table and the 540 revision 0 table.

struct.name: LD0_DMA0
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.30 Table 2-12
struct.doc: DMA channel select 0: bits 2:0, 4 means none. Read only.

struct.name: LD0_DMA1
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.30 Table 2-12
struct.doc: DMA channel select 1: bits 2:0, 4 means none. Read only.

struct.name: LD0_CONFIG
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.36

struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.33 Table 2-19
struct.doc: Base address bits 15:8.

struct.name: LD7_BASE_LSB
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.33 Table 2-19
struct.doc: Base address bits 7:0; the low bits are read only and the decoder ignores them.

struct.name: LD7_DMA0
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.33 Table 2-19
struct.doc: DMA channel select 0: bits 2:0, 4 means none. Read only.

struct.name: LD7_DMA1
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.33 Table 2-19
struct.doc: DMA channel select 1: bits 2:0, 4 means none. Read only.

struct.name: LD8_ACTIVATE
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.34 Table 2-20
struct.doc: Activate (bit 0). The PROM and Linux write the base 0xfc8 and activate it; Linux and the PROM then write function enable register 2. When clear, the power management registers are not accessible but are kept.

struct.name: LD8_IORC
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.34 Table 2-20
struct.doc: I/O range check: bit 0 chooses the byte the device drives (0xaa or 0x55) and bit 1 enables the check, valid only while the device is inactive. Bits 7:2 read 0.

struct.name: LD8_BASE_MSB
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.34 Table 2-20
struct.doc: Base address bits 15:8.

struct.name: LD8_BASE_LSB
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.34 Table 2-20
struct.doc: Base address bits 7:0; the low bits are read only and the decoder ignores them.

struct.name: LD8_DMA0
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.34 Table 2-20
struct.doc: DMA channel select 0: bits 2:0, 4 means none. Read only.

struct.name: LD8_DMA1
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.34 Table 2-20
struct.doc: DMA channel select 1: bits 2:0, 4 means none. Read only.

struct.name: FER1
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.173
struct.doc: Function enable register 1. A logical device is active only while its activate bit and its enable bit here are both set. Hardware resets it to 0xff.

struct.name: FER2
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.173-174
struct.doc: Function enable register 2. Linux and the PROM write bit 7 set (Linux's comment: it enables access to the GPIO registers). Hardware resets it to 0xff according to Table 9-1's bitmap and the text of 9.2.4; the text for bit 7 marks the cleared state as the default, which contradicts that. The PC87317 sibling datasheet resets the bit to 1.

struct.name: PMC1
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.174
struct.doc: Power management control 1: tri-state controls for the floppy, parallel and UART pins, ORed with the logical devices' own bits.

struct.name: PMC2
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.174
struct.doc: Power management control 2: clock source and clock multiplier. Bits 2:0 follow the CFG3 and CFG2 straps at reset, whose board settings are not known.

struct.name: PMC3
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.175
struct.doc: Power management control 3: parallel port, UART2 and UART1 clock enables (ANDed with the devices' own bits) and read-only busy flags.

struct.name: WDTO
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.175
struct.doc: Watchdog time-out in minutes; 0 stops the watchdog. Also cleared when the power management device is activated.

struct.name: WDCF
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.175-176
struct.doc: Watchdog configuration: which interrupts reload the timer.

struct.name: WDST
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.176
struct.doc: Watchdog status. Bit 0 is the watchdog output (1 inactive). Section 9.1.2 says bit 1; the register description and bitmap say bit 0. Whether the output reaches anything on the board is not known.

struct.name: PM_INDEX
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.172
struct.doc: Power management index register: selects the register the data port reaches. Bits 7:3 read 0.

struct.name: PM_DATA
struct.from: National Semiconductor PC87307/PC97307 datasheet (Preliminary, March 1998) p.172-173
struct.doc: Power management data register.
